transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, so... what finally made me come in today is that I keep turning in applications and research notes with these small but embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll mislabel an artwork date or just completely skip a question on a form. And the frustrating part is that I honestly thought I had checked everything over before submitting it. It just keeps happening, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself about the mistakes, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. And I'm still really interested in my art history stuff and everything I normally like doing. It's just the details that are tripping me up.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively worried or anxious about things, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?

Not really, no. I mean, obviously I get a little stressed out if I realize I just sent in a form with a bunch of errors on it, but there's a clear reason for that. I don't really have that feeling of just being anxious out of nowhere.
Do you find it hard to pay attention or stay focused on things in other areas of your life, like conversations or even when you're reading something you're interested in?

No, I haven't really noticed that. If I'm reading something I'm actually interested in, I can focus on it just fine. And, um, conversations are fine too, I don't really zone out or anything. It's really just those little details on paperwork or forms that I seem to gloss over.
Do you ever find yourself acting quickly without thinking things through, like making snap decisions or interrupting others unintentionally?

No, not really. I don't think I do that. I'm usually pretty careful about thinking things through before I act, and I definitely don't interrupt people. It's really just the careless mistakes with details that I struggle with.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of mistakes happening? Were you making similar errors when you were younger, like in school or as a child?

Yeah, it's actually been happening for a while. Um, even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I had good ideas, but I always forgot to turn in worksheets or I'd lose the instructions for things. I missed little details a lot back then, too. It was really only kept in check because my parents had to go through my backpack every single night.
Do you notice these kinds of mistakes or forgetfulness happening in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends, or is it mostly just when you're working on forms or paperwork?

Yeah, it definitely happens outside of just paperwork. I'll, um, I'll mean to do normal adult things, you know? Like returning an email, paying a bill, or just picking up groceries. And then... I don't know, days later I'll realize I never actually did it. It just completely drops out of my mind. So, yeah, it definitely affects things at home too.
Do you also find yourself forgetting or missing details in social situations or during academic tasks, like remembering appointments, following discussions, or keeping track of assignments?

Um, not really. I haven't noticed it being an issue in social situations—I can follow conversations with my friends just fine, and I don't think I miss details there. And for things like appointments or assignments, I usually put those in my phone calendar right away, so I don't really miss them either. It's mostly just the everyday tasks and paperwork I mentioned earlier that I end up forgetting.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted or having trouble staying focused during tasks that require sustained mental effort, like writing a paper or studying for an exam?

Yeah, definitely. If I know a task is going to take real concentration—like, say, drafting a curatorial proposal or having to read a really dense theory chapter for class—I'll just put it off. I'll find smaller errands to do instead, just to avoid it. And then, before I know it, it's suddenly the night before it's due and I'm scrambling to get it done.
Have you noticed these issues with focus and forgetfulness in different areas of your life, like at work, at home, and in school, or do they mostly happen in just one setting?

Yeah, it's pretty much across the board. I mean, I definitely struggle with the paperwork and putting off big assignments for school, like I mentioned. But it happens at home too, with the chores and bills just slipping my mind. So, yeah, it's not just in one place—it kind of affects a little bit of everything, whether I'm dealing with school stuff, work-like tasks, or just trying to manage things at my apartment.
Can you describe how these issues with focus and forgetfulness affect your daily routine at home, and whether you notice them impacting your performance or interactions at work or school as well?

Well, at home, it just means my apartment is usually a mess and my bills might get paid a few days late. But at school and with the art stuff I'm trying to do... it's definitely causing some problems. Because I put things off or forget the paperwork, I've ended up submitting my coursework late a few times. I've also completely missed a couple of important application deadlines for internships and grants. It actually got to the point where one of my mentors pulled me aside. They told me that my lack of follow-through is starting to hurt my chances at opportunities I should be ready for. So, yeah, it's definitely impacting my performance.
Looking back, were you already struggling with forgetfulness or difficulty focusing in multiple areas of your life, like both at school and at home, when you were a child?

Yeah, I was. Even back in elementary school, it was an issue. My teachers would always write on my report cards that I had good ideas, but I'd forget to turn in my worksheets or I'd lose the instructions for things. I was always missing those little details. Honestly, the only way I got through it back then was because my parents would check my backpack every single night to make sure I had everything I needed.
Do you ever find yourself forgetting details or losing track of things during social activities or extracurricular hobbies, like art groups or other gatherings with friends?

Um, not really, no. When it comes to just hanging out with friends or doing my art for fun, I don't really notice myself losing track of things. I guess because it's more relaxed and I'm actually into what we're doing, I don't have those same issues like I do with schoolwork or chores. So, yeah, socially, I don't think it's really a problem.
